description: Shared synthetic accounting-calendar cases for the Python traffic_models oracle and the Go accounting.Calendar target. Each case gives an explicit instant, an explicit IANA zone and an explicit billing day; expected values are pinned. Cycle keys name the month in which the cycle starts.

cases.name: utc-billing-day-1-midmonth
cases.description: A plain UTC month with the default billing day.

cases.name: utc-billing-day-3-before-start
cases.description: The second still belongs to the cycle that opened last month.

cases.name: utc-billing-day-3-on-start
cases.description: The third opens a new cycle.

cases.name: utc-year-end-billing-day-31
cases.description: A late-December boundary crosses into the next year.

cases.name: utc-year-start-billing-day-31
cases.description: New Year's Day still belongs to the cycle that started in December.

cases.name: utc-short-month-billing-day-30
cases.description: September has no 31st, so day 30 is a boundary.

cases.name: utc-short-month-billing-day-31-before
cases.description: April's clamped 31st boundary has not arrived on the 29th.

cases.name: utc-short-month-billing-day-31-on-clamp
cases.description: April's 31st billing day is clamped to the 30th.

cases.name: utc-leap-february-billing-day-29
cases.description: Leap February has a real 29th boundary.

cases.name: utc-leap-february-billing-day-30
cases.description: A 30th billing day clamps to leap February's 29th.

cases.name: utc-leap-february-billing-day-31-before
cases.description: Before leap February's clamped boundary, the cycle started in January.

cases.name: utc-nonleap-february-billing-day-28
cases.description: A 28th billing day lands exactly on non-leap February's last day.

cases.name: utc-nonleap-february-billing-day-29
cases.description: A 29th billing day clamps to non-leap February's 28th.

cases.name: utc-nonleap-february-billing-day-30-before
cases.description: The day before a clamped short-month boundary belongs to the previous cycle.

cases.name: utc-nonleap-february-billing-day-31-on-clamp
cases.description: A 31st billing day clamps to non-leap February's 28th.

cases.name: shanghai-local-midnight-before
cases.description: One second before local midnight is still the previous Shanghai day.

cases.name: shanghai-local-midnight-after
cases.description: UTC 16:00 is the next local day and opens the next Shanghai cycle.

cases.name: shanghai-local-year-boundary
cases.description: The Shanghai local date reaches the next year before UTC does.

cases.name: new-york-spring-before-transition
cases.description: The last second before the New York spring transition.

cases.name: new-york-spring-after-transition
cases.description: The first second after the New York spring transition keeps the same civil date.

cases.name: new-york-fall-before-transition
cases.description: The first occurrence of the repeated New York fall hour.

cases.name: new-york-fall-after-transition
cases.description: The second occurrence of the repeated New York fall hour keeps the same cycle.

cases.name: santiago-before-skipped-midnight
cases.description: The last instant before Santiago skips local midnight.

cases.name: santiago-skipped-local-midnight
cases.description: Santiago jumps from 23:59:59 to 01:00, so the cycle opens on the 6th, not the 5th.

cases.name: new-york-spring-midnight-after-transition
cases.description: After the spring transition, local midnight is EDT (UTC-4); fixed EST would still read March 8.

cases.name: new-york-fall-midnight-after-transition
cases.description: After the fall transition, local midnight is EST (UTC-5); fixed EDT would still read November 2.

cases.name: santiago-midnight-after-skipped-midnight
cases.description: After Santiago's skipped midnight, local midnight is UTC-3; fixed UTC-4 would still read September 6.
